_about: Q-learning, the best checkpoint of each training run: the camera-ready's learned viewing policies (appendix "Learned viewing policies", label supp:learned-policies), copied exactly on 2026-10-26 from its export paper/exports/learned_policies.json (commit 5bb3e45c; still equal at 74d92df8 on 2026-10-27) (the learned entry with objective q_regression and selection validation, and its recipe and training_time) until that export is on this branch. A viewing policy trained with reinforcement learning on top of the frozen, released CanViT-B and its frozen ADE20K linear probe (64 x 64 canvas, 512 px scenes); ADE20K validation mIoU as fractions (per_timestep, t from 0), the mean across 8 training runs with its 95% bootstrap confidence interval, evaluated with the paper's protocol. Every rollout starts with the full-scene glimpse (t = 0), as C2F's and EG-C2F's do. The reward is the relative reduction in segmentation cross-entropy after each glimpse; the policy chooses each later glimpse among 512 candidate viewpoints. Training: 8,000 steps of 16 ADE20K training images with 5 glimpses each (640,000 glimpses), 74.3 to 90.5 minutes per run on one RTX 4090, validation included. Baselines on the slide come from the paper's export (assets/paper/ade20k_seg.json), not from this file.
